clue.text: Silly commander, one showing weapon

parts.note: a silly person is an ass
an aga is a Turkish military commander
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A foolish officer shows off his weapon on parade.
explanation.definitionFit: An assagai is a slender iron-tipped spear used in southern Africa.

clue.text: Address bill, having amount to be paid

parts.note: AC is short for account, which is a bill
the cost is the price to pay

explanation.surface: Talking to someone about an invoice and how much is owed.
explanation.definitionFit: To accost someone is to approach and speak to them, often boldly.

clue.text: Celebrate with the French bachelor?

parts.note: to sing of something is to celebrate it
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's stag party, with toasts to an unmarried man.
explanation.definitionFit: A bachelor is an unmarried man; the question mark flags it as one example of the type.

clue.text: Audible complaint's increased

indicators.note: audible tells us the word is heard rather than seen, so its sound matters

parts.note: a groan is a complaint

explanation.surface: A grumble you can hear has got louder.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that has grown has become bigger or more.

clue.text: Italian shows disrespect for national anthem? That seems impossible

parts.note: It is short for Italian, as in gin and It
a person who stays seated during an anthem does not rise

explanation.surface: A disrespectful Italian at a football match, seated through the anthem.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is said of an argument or story that is not credible, which is unbelievable.

clue.text: Rubbish heap fine female falls into

indicators.note: the two single letters drop into the middle of the heap word, like things falling into a pile

parts.note: a heap is a pile
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A woman tumbles into a rubbish heap on an otherwise fine day.
explanation.definitionFit: Piffle is nonsense talk, and rubbish is a common synonym for nonsense.

clue.text: Being informed, apply to get hung at the Royal Academy?

definitions.meaning: told the relevant facts, as a past participle

definitions.text: apply to get hung at the Royal Academy?
definitions.meaning: a painter applying to the Royal Academy wants their work placed on its walls

explanation.surface: An artist told the rules for submitting work to a London gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Academy in London holds a famous annual summer exhibition of paintings.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to brief someone; literally it is placing an image within a painting.

clue.text: Enemy holding rule, king seen as stranger

indicators.note: the enemy word holds the rule word inside it

parts.note: a foe is an enemy
to reign is to rule
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A hostile king ruling a land, regarded as an outsider.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from another country is often unfamiliar, so is a stranger.

clue.text: Lounge with one old man that's sweet

parts.note: to loll is to lounge about
the Roman numeral for one is I
pop is informal for father, one's old man

explanation.surface: Dad lounging about with a sugary treat.
explanation.definitionFit: A lollipop is a hard candy on a stick, a type of confectionery.

clue.text: Opposing line put by party, its odd characters not seen to be in agreement

indicators.note: the second piece is placed beside the first in order

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
a cord is a line or string

indicators.note: the first, third and fifth letters of the word party are dropped, leaving only its even letters

explanation.surface: A rival faction's policy line clashes with a party, though its oddballs stay out of sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'its' refers back to party: removing the odd letters of PARTY leaves AT.
explanation.definitionFit: A concordat is a formal agreement, especially between the Vatican and a state.

clue.text: Top person that has to be absolutely straight

definitions.meaning: a sovereign or head of state sits at the top

definitions.text: that has to be absolutely straight
definitions.meaning: a measuring stick for drawing lines must be perfectly straight

explanation.surface: A leader is expected to be completely honest.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a monarch; the other is the straight-edged stick used for measuring and drawing lines.

clue.text: Coastal city should expel its extreme characters, OK!

indicators.note: the first and last letters of the city are thrown out

parts.note: Brighton is a seaside city on England's south coast

explanation.surface: A seaside town ought to throw out its eccentrics, all right!
explanation.walkthrough: 'extreme characters' sounds like eccentric people but means end letters.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a cheery British exclamation of agreement, like 'all right'.

clue.text: What is golden is brought back by man to church

indicators.note: the little word is is turned to read backwards

parts.note: Len is a man's name
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Something golden is returned by a man to his church.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'speech is silver, silence is golden' supplies the definition; 'brought back' turns IS into SI.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says that keeping quiet is golden, so the thing described is quietness.

clue.text: Fixing any number suffering from e.g. flu

parts.note: N is the mathematical symbol for an unspecified number
someone with flu is ailing, unwell

explanation.surface: A doctor treating any number of patients who are down with flu.
explanation.definitionFit: Nailing something means fastening or fixing it, literally with nails or figuratively.

clue.text: Healthy food, a prominent feature with disease spreading

parts.note: bran is a fibre-rich health food
a chin is a facial feature that can be prominent
gout is a disease of the joints

explanation.surface: A health food, a jutting jaw and an illness that is spreading.
explanation.definitionFit: Branching out means expanding or diversifying into new areas, so spreading outward.

clue.text: Phone criminal? It's impossible to get through

parts.note: to ring is to phone
a fence is a criminal who receives stolen goods

explanation.surface: Calling a crook and finding the line constantly engaged.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrier placed all round something, protecting it so that nothing can breach it.

clue.text: Second angry speech? Such may be cutting

parts.note: to have words is to argue angrily

explanation.surface: Another bitter exchange, with remarks that may cut deep.
explanation.definitionFit: Blades are cutting weapons, while the surface plays on cutting remarks.

clue.text: Establishes home, say, overlooking Sidmouth's front

indicators.note: in a down answer, the earlier pieces sit above the letter that follows

parts.note: in means at home
to state is to say

indicators.note: only the front letter of the Devon town's name is taken

explanation.surface: Setting up house in a property overlooking the seafront at Sidmouth.
explanation.walkthrough: Sidmouth is a seaside town in Devon. In a down clue 'overlooking' means sitting above, so INSTATE comes before S.
explanation.definitionFit: To instate someone is to install or establish them in an office or position.

clue.text: New US prisons with new configuration gain distinction

indicators.note: the letters are given a fresh arrangement, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: American jails given a new layout earn a commendation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with new configuration' shuffles NEW plus USPRISONS together.
explanation.definitionFit: Winning one's spurs is an idiom from knighthood meaning to earn honour or recognition.

clue.text: Venison at university, served up as mashed food

indicators.note: in a down answer, served up means the letters are written upward, from bottom to top

parts.note: venison is deer meat, here standing for the animal
up means in residence at university

explanation.surface: Game meat dished up at a college dinner as a soft purée.
explanation.definitionFit: Pureed food is a smooth mash of cooked ingredients.

clue.text: Aspire to reform the old country

indicators.note: to reform is to form again, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Hoping to modernise one's ancestral homeland.
explanation.definitionFit: Persia is the former name of Iran, so a country of old.

clue.text: Sweet drink at a fair is disgusting

indicators.note: something disgusting is turned upside down, upsetting the order of the letters

explanation.surface: A sugary beverage sold at a funfair is revolting.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratafia is a sweet almond-flavoured liqueur or cordial.

clue.text: Change journey to and from work

definitions.meaning: to reduce a sentence or exchange one thing for another
the daily trip between home and office

explanation.surface: Switch your route for getting to the office.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to exchange or lessen a penalty; the noun is the daily travel to a workplace.

clue.text: Partner not wanting English church for marriage

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the letter is left out

parts.note: a mate is a partner

explanation.surface: A spouse who would rather not wed in an Anglican church.
explanation.definitionFit: A match is a pairing, especially a marriage between two people.

clue.text: Locatin' a demonstration

definitions.meaning: locating means siting; the apostrophe drops its final G, as in casual speech
a protest where people occupy a place and refuse to leave

explanation.surface: A slangy word for finding a place, followed by a protest.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'Locatin'' tells the solver to drop the G of the synonym too.
explanation.definitionFit: A sit-in is a protest where people occupy a place and refuse to leave.

clue.text: A certain Thomas was encouraged to, unquestionably

definitions.text: A certain Thomas was encouraged to
definitions.meaning: Doubting Thomas, the apostle, was urged by Jesus to stop questioning, to have less scepticism

explanation.surface: A sceptical man named Thomas was urged to stop questioning.
explanation.walkthrough: Doubting Thomas is the apostle who would not believe in the resurrection until he saw the wounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean without question or certainly, as adverbs.

clue.text: Dreaming, maybe, like backward-looking PM of yesteryear

parts.note: as means like, in the sense of in the manner of

indicators.note: the prime minister's name is read from end to start

parts.note: Sir Robert Peel was a 19th-century British prime minister

explanation.surface: Like a nostalgic former prime minister, lost in dreams.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone dreaming is an example of a person in slumber, hence the 'maybe'.

clue.text: Bit of rubbish heaped untidily in shrub

indicators.note: only a small bit of the word, its opening letter, is used

explanation.surface: Some rubbish heaped messily in a bush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'untidily' rearranges R (first of rubbish) with HEAPED.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephedra is a genus of jointed shrubs, the source of the drug ephedrine.
